newsitem.title: USA: Texas Instruments reports lower earnings.
newsitem.headline: Texas Instruments reports lower earnings.

text.p: Texas Instruments Inc., reported lower first quarter earnings Tuesday, but said semiconductor orders grew sharply in the first quarter and pointed to strong demand for new chips as the market recovers from a dismal 1996.

Dallas-based Texas Instruments reported first quarter earnings of $129 million, or 66 cents a share, on revenues of $2.26 billion. A year earlier it earned $163 million, or 84 cents a share, on revenues of $2.67 billion.
Texas Instruments said, however, that semiconductor orders in the quarter grew at double-digit rates over the fourth quarter of 1996, "with strength across all products and geographic regions."

While first quarter revenues from DRAM (dynamic random access memory) chips, one of the most common chips, were lower than a year ago due to lower prices, other semiconductor revenues were significantly higher, Texas Instruments said.

The company said semiconductor inventories remained at record low levels and it was seeing signs of improved stability in DRAM pricing. It was the collapse of DRAM prices last year that battered the global chip market.
The company said it expected the world semiconductor market to grow about 10 percent this year, following a decline of 9 percent in 1996.

It said revenue growth in so-called differentiated products such as digital signal processors and mixed-signal/analog products continued to surge, and those products also showed higher operating profit margins.
Digital signal processors are chip which translate sounds and sight into digital form and are used in cellular phones, modems and digital video among other uses.
Digital signal processors and mixed-signal/analog products will continue to grow two or three times faster than the overall market, it said.

Texas Instruments said orders for digital signal processors reached record levels in the first quarter, with particular strength in mass storage, networking and wireless communications end equipment markets. Revenues from those products accounted for more than 40 percent of total semiconductor revenues.
Chief Executive Officer Tom Engibous said the company would continue to focus on differentiated products.
"Our strong leadership position in digital signal processing solutions provides significant competitive advantage to us and to our customers," he said.

"The opportunity we have today in DSPs (digital signal processors) is the biggest opportunity for TI since the invention of the integrated circuit ... This particular business has great potential to accelerate TI's move toward higher value, higher growth and better financial stability."
Texas Instruments stock was up $2.375 at $85.50 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
